A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAM/GGD-BAM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across substantial relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling perplexity, passkey-retrieval accuracy, attention visualizations, and initialization, parameter-learning, and training-length ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds short-context perplexity, RULER retrieval evaluations, larger-model experiments, context-extension comparisons, and inference timings.

M1.justification: The GGD attention bias, parameterization, and SSMax combination remain unchanged. v2 introduces a context-extension adaptation: continuing initial 512-token training for 256 steps at length 1024 to improve larger-model extrapolation (Appendices C and F.5).

E1.justification: v2 adds the NIAH subset of RULER, extending the original passkey task to Single 1–3, including UUID retrieval, and MultiKey, MultiQuery, and MultiValue requirements (Appendix E). FineWeb, Wikipedia, and the original passkey evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: The external PE baseline families and SSMax variants are retained. Within the parameter-learning comparison, however, v2 Figure 9 adds Fixed and θα-plus-θµ-only BAM controls to the three configurations shown in v1 Figure 8. The new large-model comparisons use the existing RoPE SSMax baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds approximately 430M and 1.1B model configurations, size-specific learning rates, and the 256-step context-extension stage. New evaluations include held-out sequences up to 512 tokens, RULER context-length grids, and forward-pass timing at batch size 1 and length 512 across four sizes, including an 8B-sized configuration used only for timing.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original ablations, v2 adds fixed-parameter and θα-plus-θµ controls (Figure 9), context-extension comparisons across model sizes (Table 5), a 1.1B BAM–RoPE passkey comparison (Figure 14), and inference-cost analysis (Table 6). These investigate learnability, scaling failures, their mitigation, and computational overhead.

E5.justification: v1 provides no comparable uncertainty reporting. v2 Appendix F.7 reports 100 timing samples and Table 6 includes standard deviations alongside execution times. Neither version reports comparable repeated-training or seed-based uncertainty for retrieval accuracy and perplexity.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark curves are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial result sets in Tables 2–6 and Figure 14, plus two parameter-ablation curves. For example, the new large-model RULER Single 1 comparison reports accuracy 1.00 for BAM SSMax versus 0.00 for RoPE SSMax at 32,768 tokens. These are newly evaluated settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 switches Z from a multiplier to a denominator, preserving the underlying attention identity. However, the revision is propagated inconsistently: Appendix I.1 equates the overlap sum with its reciprocal partition-function ratio, and I.2 retains an incompatible multiplicative renormalization identity. v1 Appendix G used the reciprocal consistently in these identities. Other substantive proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: probabilistic unification of positional encoding, the Generalized Gaussian prior, retrieval at approximately 500 times training length, and comparable perplexity with minimal extra parameters. The new experiments support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 introduces training-length overfitting as an explanation for larger-model failures, context extension as a remedy, and interpretations of difficult RULER tasks and inference overhead. The scale limitation shifts from approximately 125M to 1.1B parameters. Some summaries overgeneralize: the stated RULER superiority has exceptions, including Table 3 Single 2 at 4K, where RoPE SSMax scores 0.52 versus BAM SSMax's 0.24.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Table 1 substantially extend the reproduction recipe with larger-model layer, head, width, feed-forward, and learning-rate specifications and the additional context-extension stage. v2 also documents the timing procedure and identifies Wikipedia snapshot 20231101.en. The original BAM implementation formula, hardware description, and code-access link remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Singh and Buckley on expectation-based attention, Han and Ji on positional generalization, and Hsieh et al. for RULER. Its RoPE discussion changes from emphasizing difficult content–position factorization to describing asymptotic approximation of BAM. The broader related-work structure is retained.

P1.justification: The perplexity discussion moves from the main text into Appendix D, attention-head analysis becomes Section 3.2, and appendix experiments are regrouped. There are localized wording corrections, author-line changes, and a switch to author–year citations. Most existing prose, including the abstract and conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds five result tables and the large-model heatmaps, expands the architecture table, and adds two curves to the parameter ablation. The original retrieval heatmap is redrawn with a different color scale and marginal averages; perplexity figures are relocated. Typography, headings, and page headers also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The RULER evaluations and controlled scaling/context-extension comparisons address part of v1's restricted empirical validation and clarify conditions under which extrapolation succeeds or fails. These improve the paper's assessability. The net gain is limited by new summaries that overstate the tables and inconsistent Z identities introduced in Appendix I, which weaken reporting precision and theoretical clarity.
